pull_request.title: Tracker: Establish the service-constrained working baseline
pull_request.head: study/tracker-service-optimization
pull_request.body:
The user selected the **original-pocket layout as the new tracker working baseline on 2026-09-30**. This PR records that choice and the service-constrained placement study behind it. It is the follow-up to #25; engineering qualification and formal production sign-off are outstanding.

The selected case is **`p190-s680-b1-l1287.33-front_loaded-original-pockets`**. [DES-011 SO-C19 records the human instruction, exact geometry hash and retained configuration](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/655f47e44725a7aa30d8d9bd46266131254001b8/docs/design/DES-011-service-constrained-tracker-optimization.md#working-baseline-selected-on-2026-09-30).

With silicon area no longer a driving concern, this layout retains more service space and avoids increased zero-hit fractions in the measured bins for only a 0.64% reduction in mean stations relative to the compact coverage candidate. It yields **9.0182 mean usable stations**, **197.250 m² physical silicon** and **1009.57 mm worst-mode p95 maximum inter-station gap**. Relative to PR #25, mean stations improve by 9.6% and that gap statistic decreases by 26.8%.

The baseline retains:

- Barrel radii: pixels **34/60/106/182 mm**, short strips **260/340/480/660 mm**, long strips **840/1060 mm**.
- **23 long-strip rows at the inherited pitch**, including the central row, and front-loaded endcaps.
- Constant pixel/short/long service trunks **44/73/25 mm**, larger original routing pockets, and positive first-disc centres **611.7/1295.5/1403.65 mm**.
- The **tested final-disc bypass**, complete downstream inventory and inherited module/staggering/local-tilt choices. No inclined barrel section is introduced.

Removing the bypass is a separate simplification study requiring matched dense/native validation. The area/coverage alternatives and rejected spacing candidate remain visible; selecting a working baseline does not alter the frozen training rankings or retained numerical evidence.

[Results, per-subdetector tables, selected-baseline routing mockups and repeatable workflow](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/655f47e44725a7aa30d8d9bd46266131254001b8/docs/validation/DES-011-service-constrained-optimization.md).

The study corrects and preserves two rejected runs: a central seam from 24 barrel rows, and pockets that passed area capacity but could not contain the adopted 13.4 mm cable. The final corrected execution covers eight primary cases plus three comparisons, with local-coverage and individual-component route/throat gates.

Retained validation: **136 module tests (133 passed, 3 ACTS-dependent system-Python skips)**; **360/360 actual ACTS trajectories agree**; 180,960 final mode-track evaluations; inventory, fit, capacity and local-coverage audits; 22 PNG/PDF views. This baseline-record update changes no numerical geometry, code or configuration: its geometry hash, unchanged evidence, dashboard build and session logs were checked.

Conservative/stress service scenarios still fail. Connector/bend envelopes, support/cooling interfaces, service material and vessel access are the next engineering priorities. Measured-bin coverage is not proof of continuum hermeticity. DES-011 remains DRAFT/PROTOTYPE; PR #24's historical layout was not retrospectively approved.

User asks for at most two pixel-barrel support/cooling candidates, minimizing
material while providing stability and sufficient cooling, with technical drawings
and literature cross-checks. The request cites PR26; inspection finds infrastructure
branch restoration there. The preceding human-selected baseline is PR28, and this
interpretation was communicated before continuing. The baseline is unchanged.

The branch starts from the PR28 merge on `study/tracker-service-corridors`; local
and remote main still contained the older PR25 geometry. Unrelated usage-summary
files were preserved. DES002 was planned in PROJECT but had no existing design
file; this task supplies it as DRAFT/PROTOTYPE, with no sign-off.
